definitions.explanation: A type of semi-oxidized Chinese tea, positioned between green tea and black tea in terms of oxidation. In Japan, usually refers to oolong tea as a beverage, especially the bottled or canned variety widely available in vending machines and convenience stores.

examples.japanese: {烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ}を{一|ひと}つください。
{食事|しょくじ}のときはいつも{烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}んでいる。
examples.english: I always drink oolong tea with meals.

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}で{車|くるま}の{運転|うんてん}があるので{烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ}を{頼|たの}んだら、「ウーロンハイにしますか」と{聞|き}かれた。
examples.english: At the izakaya I ordered oolong tea because I was driving, and they asked if I wanted an oolong highball instead.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always appears in the compound {烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ} (oolong tea). The word {烏龍|うーろん} alone is rarely used. Often written in katakana as ウーロン{茶|ちゃ}.

{烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ} is one of the most popular non-alcoholic beverages in Japan. It is a standard drink option at restaurants and izakaya, and is widely available in PET bottles and cans from vending machines.

DRINK COMPOUNDS:
- {烏龍|うーろん}{茶|ちゃ}: oolong tea
- ウーロンハイ: oolong highball ({焼酎|しょうちゅう} mixed with oolong tea)

ETYMOLOGY:
From Chinese {烏龍|うーろん} (wulong), literally "black dragon," referring to the dark, twisted appearance of the tea leaves.
